speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis. The clinical presentation of pain localized to the weight-bearing joints (hips, knees) and the first metatarsophalangeal joint (big toe), characterized by worsening with activity and improvement with rest, is classic for osteoarthritis. The absence of prolonged morning stiffness and the specific involvement of the "big toe" (often misidentified as gouty but here fitting the pattern of hallux rigidus/OA in an older male with multiple joint OA) further support this over inflammatory arthritis or gout.
